Approaching from the left, we have x<π, so we use the expression f(x)=(x−π+3)2. We get limx→π−f(x)=limx→π−(x−π+3)2=(π−π+3)2=(3)2=3.

Approaching from the right, we have x≥π, so we use the expression f(x)=5+2cos⁡(x) We get limx→π+f(x)=limx→π+(5+2cos⁡(x))=5+2cos⁡(π)=5+2(−1)=3.

Therefore, we conclude that limx→π−f(x)=limx→π+f(x)=3.

2.?

Find the left- and right-sided limits at x=0 of the piecewise function f(x) defined by f(x)={−x+1 for x≤0sin⁡x+1 for x>0.

Sat, Aug 8th @ 7:33 PM|Elapsed: 0:35Correct

Approaching from the left, we have x<0, so we use the expression f(x)=−x+1. We get

limx→0−f(x)=limx→0−(−x+1)=−(0)+1=1.

Now, approaching from the right, we have x>0, so we use the expression f(x)=sin⁡x+1. We get

limx→0+f(x)=limx→0+sin⁡x+1=sin⁡0+1=0+1=1.

Therefore, we conclude that limx→0−f(x)=limx→0+f(x)=1.
